extracted.intended_audience: authors, performers, producers, broadcasting organizations, inventors, IP applicants, IP practitioners and rights holders in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory standards from Vietnamese law covering copyrights, related rights, registration and industrial property (inventions, designs, layout-designs, marks, trade names, geographical indications). Specifies eligibility, exclusions, definitions, procedural and contractual requirements for protection and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses of related rights not requiring permission or remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: The following forms of use of related rights shall not require obtaining permission and paying royalties and remuneration:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a) Duplication by oneself of one single copy of works for the purpose of personal scientific research; b) Duplication by oneself of one single copy of works for the purpose of teaching activities, except when phonograms, or broadcasting programs have been published for teaching; c) Reasonable quotation the purpose of providing information only; d) A broadcasting organization temporarily makes a phonogram by itself for broadcasting when it is entitled to the right to broadcast. Persons using these rights must not affect normal exploitation or prejudice rights of performers, phonogram producers or broadcasting organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of related rights without permission but requiring royalties/remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations and individuals using related rights in certain commercial cases shall not be liable for obtaining permission but shall be liable to pay royalties or remunerations as agreed:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a) Directly or indirectly using a published sound/video recording for commercial purpose to carry out broadcasting programs with sponsorship, advertisements or collection of money; b) Using a published sound/video recording in their business and commercial activities. Such use must not influence normal exploitation or prejudice rights of performers, producers or broadcasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of related rights protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of protection for related rights is 50 years following the year of fixation/publication/broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Performer rights: 50 years from year of fixation of the performance. 2) Producer of phonograms: 50 years from year of publication, or 50 years from fixation if not published. 3) Broadcasting organization: 50 years from year of broadcast. Terms end at 24:00 on 31 December of the year the term ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related rights infringement acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated acts that constitute infringement of related rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: abrogating rights of performers/producers/broadcasting organizations; assuming names of performers/producers/broadcasters; publishing/producing/communicating fixed performances/phonograms/broadcasts without permission; modifying/mutilating/distorting performances prejudicing honor and prestige; reproducing/extracting fixed performances/phonograms/broadcasts without permission; removing/altering right management information in electronic format without permission; intentionally canceling/invalidating technical protection methods; distributing/importing/broadcasting/communicating material when knowing right management info was removed/altered; producing/assembling/transforming/distributing/importing/exporting/selling/renting equipment used for illegal decoding of encrypted satellite signals; intentionally recording/disseminating satellite signals decoded without permission of lawful distributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright owner: author
rubrics_metrics.description: An author who creates his work by using his own time, finance and other physical and technical facilities shall have the rights stipulated in Articles 19 and 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author is default copyright owner unless otherwise agreed or assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright owner: co-author
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-author who co-creates a work by using his own time, finance and other material conditions shall have personal and property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where co-authored works consist of separable parts, each co-author has rights over their separate part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright owner: employer or contracting organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization that assigns a duty of creating a work to an employee shall be the owner of rights, except where otherwise agreed; similarly for contracted works unless otherwise agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership follows written agreement; default rule vests employer/contracting organization with rights stipulated in Articles 20 and 19.3 unless contract provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright owner: heir and assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: Heirs under inheritance law and assignees by contract may be copyright owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heirs acquire rights according to inheritance law; assignees acquire rights as agreed in contract over parts or whole of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-owned works
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain works are state-owned: posthumous works; works whose owners died without heirs or where heirs waived rights; works assigned to the State by the copyright owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government will provide specific provisions on use of state-owned works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works of public domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Works whose protection terms have expired are in the public domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All organizations and individuals may use public domain works respecting authors' personal rights; Government will provide provisions on use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related right owners: performers, phonogram producers, broadcasting organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who use their own time, finance and material facilities to make a performance, phonogram, or broadcasting program are owners unless otherwise agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership may be altered by agreement with related parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of copyrights and related rights: general provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment is transfer of owner rights under contract or legislation; authors/performers cannot assign personal rights except publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment of rights in works created by co-owners requires agreement of all co-owners; where works have separable parts each owner may assign rights over their part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract requirements for assignment of copyrights/related rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract for assignment must be made in writing and include main contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main contents required: a) full name and address of assignor and assignee; b) grounds of assignment; c) price and mode of payment; d) rights and obligations of each party; d') obligations for breach of contract. Implementation/amendment/termination follow Civil Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transference (licensing) of use of copyrights/related rights: general provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transference means owner allows others to use part or whole of exclusive rights for a limited time; personal rights generally non-transferable except publication right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transference of co-authored works requires agreement of all co-authors; co-owners may transfer use of their part; licensees may sublicense with consent of owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract requirements for use (license) of copyrights/related rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract for use must be made in writing and include specified main contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main contents: a) full name and address of assignor and assignee; b) grounds of assignment; c) scope of the assignment of the right; d) price and mode of payment; d') rights and obligations of each party; e) obligations for breach of contract. Implementation/amendment/termination follow Civil Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of copyrights and related rights: nature and evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration means filing an application and attached documents with competent state authorities to attest information of author, work and owner; filing is not mandatory for entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration certificate holders are not obliged to prove rights upon dispute except where opposition proof is given. Registration is optional but provides presumptive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents for registration of copyrights/related rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall include a declaration form in Vietnamese signed by applicant/owner/authorized person and specified supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: a) declaration form with full applicant/author/owner info and summary of main contents, derivative work info, publication details and commitments; b) 02 copies of the work or fixation; c) power of attorney if authorized; d) documents evidencing right to file if obtained by inheritance/transfer/assignment; d') agreement of all co-authors if co-authored; e) agreement of all co-owners if joint ownership. Documents must be in Vietnamese or translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent authority for registration certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The State management authority in charge of copyrights and related rights issues registration certificates and has power to reissue, replace or annul them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government shall provide specific conditions, orders and procedures; Ministry shall set out forms of Certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for issuing registration certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority must grant certificate within 15 working days from receipt of valid application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If refusing to grant, authority shall notify applicant in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and territorial effect of registration certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright/Related Rights Registration Certificates are effective in the whole territory of Vietnam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates issued before the law's full force retain validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and publication of registration decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates shall be recorded in the National Register; decisions to issue/reissue/change/annul must be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public notice of registration status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue, replacement or annulment of registration certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities shall reissue or replace lost/damaged certificates or annul certificates issued to persons not the author/owner/protected subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person discovering contrary grant may request cancellation of certificate validity; authority in Article 51.2 handles such matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective management organizations: role and authorized activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective management organizations are non-profit groups established by agreement among authors/owners to protect copyrights and related rights and to manage licensing and royalties as authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities: manage rights; negotiate licensing, seizing and dividing royalties/remuneration; protect members' rights and reconcile disputes. Rights/obligations include encouraging creation, cooperating with national/international organizations, reporting to competent authorities, and other duties under law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultancy and service organizations: permitted activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultancy/service organizations operate to provide legal/IP services as requested by authors and rights owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities: legal consultancy on copyright issues; carry out registration procedures under authorization; join other legal relations and protect lawful rights under authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention patent eligibility (general requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is eligible for an Invention Patent if it is: (a) novel; (b) involves an inventive step; (c) susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are conjunctive conditions for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility solution patent eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A Utility solution Patent is eligible if it is novel and susceptible of industrial application (inventive step not required unless common knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility solution applies unless it is common knowledge; lower threshold than invention patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated exclusions from invention protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods; schemes/plans/rules/methods for mental acts/training animals/playing games/doing business; computer programs; presentations of information; solutions of aesthetic characteristics only; plant and animal varieties; essentially biological processes for production of plants/animals (other than microbiological); disease prevention/diagnostic/treatment methods for humans/animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is novel if it is not publicly disclosed by any means inside or outside the country before the filing or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not publicly disclosed if known only to a limited number obliged to keep secret. Exceptions (not lacking novelty) if published and application filed within 6 months from publication when: a) published by another person without permission of right-holder; b) published as a scientific presentation by right-holder; c) exhibited at a national or officially recognized international exhibition by right-holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, based on all prior disclosed technical solutions, it constitutes inventive progress and cannot be easily created by a person with ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers all technical solutions disclosed before filing or priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Susceptibility of industrial application (industrial applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is susceptible of industrial application if it is possible to carry out mass production or repeated application of the process and achieve stable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires practical reproducibility and stable outcomes in production or repeated application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is eligible for protection if it is new, creative, and susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three conditions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions from industrial design protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: appearance dictated by technical features of product; appearance of civil/industrial construction works; appearance of a product that is invisible during use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is new if it significantly differs from previously disclosed industrial designs before filing or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two designs are not significantly different if differences are only in features not easily noticeable/memorable and cannot distinguish the designs as a whole. Not yet publicly disclosed if known only to a limited number obliged to keep secret. Exceptions similar to inventions — 6-month grace for certain publications/exhibitions by right-holder or published without permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity of industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is creative if, based on prior publicly disclosed designs, it cannot be easily created by a person with ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates non-obviousness relative to prior public designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Susceptibility of industrial application for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design is susceptible of industrial application if it can serve as a model for mass production of a product with that appearance by industrial or handicraft methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on capacity to be reproduced at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout-design eligibility (semiconductor topographies)
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design is eligible if it is original and commercially novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to semiconductor integrated circuit layout-designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions for layout-design protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes principles/processes/systems/methods operated by semiconductor integrated circuits, and information or software contained in such circuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design is original if it results from the author's own creative effort and is not widely known among creators/manufacturers at time of creation; commonplace combinations are original only if the combination as a whole is original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality looks at creative effort and novelty among practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial novelty of layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout-design is commercially novel if it has not been commercially exploited anywhere in the world prior to the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not lacking commercial novelty if application filed within 2 years from first commercial exploitation by the right-holder or licensee. Commercial exploitation means public distribution for commercial purposes of an integrated circuit produced by incorporating the layout-design or an article incorporating such integrated circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks eligibility: basic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark is eligible if it is a visible sign (letters, words, pictures, figures, including 3D) and is capable of distinguishing goods or services of the owner from those of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks may be in one or more colors and include combinations and three-dimensional figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs not protected as marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated signs excluded from mark protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes national flags/emblems; signs identical or confusingly similar to emblems/flags/armorial bearings/official names of State agencies or political organizations (unless permitted); names/images of leaders or national heroes; certification/control/warranty seals (unless registered as certification marks); signs liable to mislead/ confuse/ deceive consumers about origin, functional parameters, purpose, quality, value or other characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of marks and non-distinctive signs
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark is distinctive if it consists of easily noticeable and memorable elements or combination and is not among excluded non-distinctive signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-distinctive signs include: simple devices and geometric figures; numerals/letters/words of uncommon languages (except widely used/recognized); signs/common names widely used and common knowledge; descriptive signs indicating time/place/method/production/kind/quantity/quality/composition/intended purpose/value/other characteristics (unless acquired distinctiveness through use); signs describing legal status/activity field; geographical indications (unless acquired distinctiveness or registered as collective/certification marks); signs identical/confusingly similar to registered marks with earlier filing/priority date; signs identical/confusingly similar to widely used recognized marks or recently terminated registrations (subject to conditions); signs similar to well-known marks that may prejudice distinctiveness; signs identical/similar to trade names likely to cause consumer confusion; signs identical/similar to geographical indications that mislead consumers; signs identical/similar to protected geographical indications for wines/spirits if registered for non-origin goods; signs identical/insignificantly different from protected industrial designs with earlier filing/priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for recognition of a well-known mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors to consider when determining whether a mark is well-known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: 1) number of related consumers aware of the mark via purchase/use/advertising; 2) territorial scope of circulation of goods/services bearing the mark; 3) turnover or volume of goods/services; 4) period of continuous use; 5) widespread goodwill; 6) number of countries granting protection; 7) number of countries recognizing it as well-known; 8) value of assignment/licensing price or investment value in respect of the mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade name eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name is eligible for protection if it is capable of distinguishing the business entity bearing it from others in the same field and locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctiveness in field and locality is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions for trade name protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations of State agencies, political/socio-political/social/socio-professional organizations or entities not engaged in business activities shall not be protected as trade names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness of trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name is distinctive if it meets certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: 1) consist of a proper name (except where widely known through use); 2) not identical or confusingly similar to a trade name used earlier in same field and locality; 3) not identical or confusingly similar to another's mark or protected geographical indication used earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indication eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A geographical indication is eligible if: 1) the product originates from the area corresponding to the indication; 2) the product has reputation, quality or characteristics essentially attributable to geographical conditions of that area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both origin and attributable reputation/quality/characteristics are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matters not protected as geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated exclusions from GI protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: designations that have become generic names in Vietnam; GIs of a foreign country not protected or no longer used; GIs identical/similar to a protected mark if use causes confusion as to origin; GIs that mislead consumers as to true geographical origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation of products having geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation shall be determined on the basis of consumers' trust in the product through the extent to which it is known and selected by consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on consumer awareness and selection as indicators of reputation (Article 81 begins this definition).
